import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 394

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/394](https://www.erdosproblems.com/394)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [ErHa78] Erdős, P. and Hall, R. R., On some unconventional problems on the divisors of integers.
  J. Austral. Math. Soc. Ser. A (1978), 479--485.
-/

open Nat Filter Finset
open scoped Asymptotics Topology Nat

namespace Erdos394

/--
Let $t_k(n)$ denote the least $m$ such that $n\mid m(m+1)(m+2)\cdots (m+k-1).$
-/
noncomputable def t (k n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf { m : ℕ | 0 < m ∧ n ∣ ∏ i ∈ range k, (m + i) }

/-- `t k n = v` when `v` works and nothing positive below it does. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem t_eq_of {n k v : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v)
    (hdvd : n ∣ ∏ i ∈ range k, (v + i))
    (hlt : ∀ m ∈ range v, 0 < m → ¬ (n ∣ ∏ i ∈ range k, (m + i))) :
    t k n = v := by
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le ⟨hv, hdvd⟩) ?_
  by_contra! hc
  have hne : { m : ℕ | 0 < m ∧ n ∣ ∏ i ∈ range k, (m + i) }.Nonempty := ⟨v, hv, hdvd⟩
  obtain ⟨hpos, hd⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem hne
  exact hlt _ (mem_range.mpr hc) hpos hd

/-- The least positive multiple of `n` is `n`, so `t 1 n = n`. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem t_one {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : t 1 n = n := by
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le ⟨hn, by simp⟩) ?_
  have hne : { m : ℕ | 0 < m ∧ n ∣ ∏ i ∈ range 1, (m + i) }.Nonempty := ⟨n, hn, by simp⟩
  obtain ⟨hpos, hd⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem hne
  rw [prod_range_one, add_zero] at hd
  exact Nat.le_of_dvd hpos hd

/--
Is it true that $\sum_{n\leq x}t_2(n)\ll \frac{x^2}{(\log x)^c}$ for some $c>0$?
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-394/Research/FirstQuestion.lean"]
theorem erdos_394.parts.i :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∃ c > 0, (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊,
      (t 2 n : ℝ)) ≪ (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 / (Real.log x) ^ c) := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that, for $k\geq 2$, $\sum_{n\leq x}t_{k+1}(n) =o\left(\sum_{n\leq x}t_k(n)\right)?$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-394/Research/DenseHierarchyLittleO.lean"]
theorem erdos_394.parts.ii :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∀ k ≥ 2, (fun (x : ℝ) ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊,
      (t (k + 1) n : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun (x : ℝ) ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊,
      (t k n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
In [ErGr80] they mention a conjecture of Erdős that the sum is $o(x^2)$. This was proved by Erdős
and Hall [ErHa78], who proved that in fact
$\sum_{n\leq x}t_2(n)\ll \frac{\log\log\log x}{\log\log x}x^2.$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.hall_bound :
    (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊, (t 2 n : ℝ)) ≪
    (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 * (Real.log (Real.log (Real.log x)) / Real.log (Real.log x))) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Hall conjecture that the sum is $o(x^2/(\log x)^c)$ for any $c<\log 2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.hall_conjecture :
    ∀ c < Real.log 2, (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊,
    (t 2 n : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
    (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 / (Real.log x) ^ c) := by
  sorry

/--
Since $t_2(p)=p-1$ for prime $p$ it is trivial that $\sum_{n\leq x}t_2(n)\gg \frac{x^2}{\log x}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 / Real.log x) ≪
    (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊, (t 2 n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
They ask about the behaviour of $t_{n-3}(n!)$ and also ask whether, for infinitely many $n$,
$t_k(n!)< t_{k-1}(n!)-1$ for all $1\leq k < n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.factorial_gap_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      Set.Infinite { n : ℕ | ∀ k, 2 ≤ k → k < n →
      t k (n !) < t (k - 1) (n !) - 1 } := by
  sorry

set_option maxRecDepth 20000 in
/--
They proved (with Selfridge) that this holds for $n=10$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.factorial_gap_10 :
    ∀ (k : ℕ), 2 ≤ k → k < 10 →
    t k (10 !) <
    t (k - 1) (10 !) - 1 := by
  have h1 : t 1 (10 !) = 3628800 := by rw [t_one] <;> norm_num [Nat.factorial]
  have h2 : t 2 (10 !) = 512000 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by native_decide) (by native_decide)
  have h3 : t 3 (10 !) = 6398 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by native_decide) (by native_decide)
  have h4 : t 4 (10 !) = 5373 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by native_decide) (by native_decide)
  have h5 : t 5 (10 !) = 348 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by decide) (by decide)
  have h6 : t 6 (10 !) = 160 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by decide) (by decide)
  have h7 : t 7 (10 !) = 30 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by decide) (by decide)
  have h8 : t 8 (10 !) = 9 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by decide) (by decide)
  have h9 : t 9 (10 !) = 2 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by decide) (by decide)
  intro k hk2 hk10
  interval_cases k <;> simp_all

end Erdos394

findings.description: The untyped exponent in `∃ c > 0` is inferred as `c : ℕ`, not `ℝ`. Thus the declaration requires a positive integer logarithmic saving. In scratch Lean I proved that this condition is equivalent to S₂(x) = O(x²/log x), rather than the requested existence of any positive real exponent. I also proved that the test growth rate x²/√(log x) satisfies the real-exponent condition with c = 1/2 but satisfies no positive-natural-exponent condition. The cited formal proof explicitly chooses c = 1/2048 and does not certify the stronger declaration as written.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/394 asks for the bound 'for some c>0'. Erdős–Hall (1978), p.481, following Theorem 3, says 'some fixed a>0' and even 'any fixed a<log 2' (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-26.pdf). The cited Research/FirstQuestion.lean proves Research.FirstQuestion, whose definition explicitly quantifies c : ℝ, using (1 : ℝ)/2048.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `∃ c > 0, ...` with `∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ...`, or equivalently `∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ...`. Keep answer(True): the cited proof establishes this corrected statement, including after restriction to the file's natural cutoffs.

findings.description: The docstring says 'for all 1 ≤ k < n', but the Lean correctly uses `2 ≤ k`. Including k=1 would invoke t₀(n!); with this definition t₀(10!)=0, making the claimed n=10 example impossible. This is a documentation error, not an error in the Lean range.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Hall, On some unconventional problems on the divisors of integers (1978), p.481, asks for 'every 1 < i ≤ n−1' and states that n=10 works with Selfridge: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-26.pdf . The website currently has the same non-strict lower-bound typo copied into the docstring.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring's `1 ≤ k < n` to `2 ≤ k < n` (equivalently `1 < k < n`). Do not broaden the Lean range.

reformulations.difference: The custom ≪ notation restricts x to ℕ, rather than allowing real cutoffs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The sum at real x equals the sum at floor x. For g(x)=x² log log log x/log log x, g(floor x)/g(x) tends to 1: floor x/x and the corresponding ratios of the iterated logarithms tend to 1. Consequently the natural-cutoff and real-cutoff O-bounds imply each other. The general iff was proved in /workspace/review/reformulations.lean.

reformulations.difference: Here too ≪ uses natural cutoffs rather than real cutoffs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For g(x)=x²/log x, g(floor x) is asymptotic to g(x), while the partial sum is unchanged by replacing x with floor x. This gives equivalence in the lower-bound direction as well. Both directions were proved in /workspace/review/reformulations.lean.

reformulations.difference: The primary paper proposes a family of O-bounds for exponents below log 2; Lean states a family of little-o bounds, matching the modern Erdős Problems page.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given c<log 2, choose max(c,0)<d<log 2. The O-bound at d implies the little-o bound at c because (log x)^(c−d) tends to zero. Conversely each little-o bound implies the corresponding O-bound. This also explains why allowing nonpositive c adds no content. Both readings of the family equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/hall_equivalence.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses natural truncated subtraction and the range 2 ≤ k < n instead of ordinary integer subtraction and the primary paper's range 1 < k ≤ n−1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For all a,b : ℕ, a < b−1 is equivalent to a+1<b and hence to (a : ℤ)<(b : ℤ)−1, including b=0 or 1. The two index ranges coincide under their lower bounds. A whole-set infinitude iff was proved in /workspace/review/factorial_equivalence.lean; the same argument applies to the n=10 instance.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/394 (including remarks; HTML retrieved through r.jina.ai after direct Cloudflare challenges)
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-26.pdf — Erdős–Hall (1978), especially p.481 and the proof of Theorem 3

https://omniscienceproject.com/research/papers/erdos-problem-394-and-the-average-order-of-t-2-a-counterexample-6CWZNbA5/pdf — Paratelligent Research Agent and Jeff Pickhardt, July 22, 2026, especially Theorem 3.10 and its proof
review.notes:
All ten declarations were checked. The minimum's defining set is nonempty for positive k,n, and its zero/empty-set defaults do not affect the substantive statements. The n=10 minima were independently computed and agree with the file; factorial_gap_10 has no sorry but uses six native_decide axioms.

Both cited affirmative proof targets were rebuilt and checked in /workspace/review/external_both_audit.lean, with only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The first certifies the corrected real-exponent statement; the second certifies the file's statement unchanged. The downloaded proof's 105 Research sources matched the pinned commit's git-blob hashes. Rebuilding with the newer sandbox toolchain required proof-only compatibility edits, with no changes to definitions or theorem statements.

The canonical page still labels #394 OPEN, despite the cited affirmative formal proofs. It also links a July 2026 manuscript claiming a disproof of hall_conjecture. That manuscript is listed only as an unverified proof claim, with an explicit disclaimer of endorsement; I have not treated that listing alone as an established status change. It is worth maintainer follow-up, but is not a mathematical misformalization of hall_conjecture.

The reviewed file was not modified.

submission.summary: Explicitly quantified the logarithmic-saving exponent over ℝ, preserving answer(True) and the existing solved/proof attributes. Also corrected the trivial, previously reported factorial-gap docstring typo to 2 ≤ k < n without changing that theorem. The required compilation succeeds with only the permitted `declaration uses sorry` warnings.
